definitions.explanation: The ability to control one's emotions, impulses, and desires. A valued personal quality in both personal and professional settings.

examples.japanese: {自制心|じせいしん}が{強|つよ}い{人|ひと}だ。
examples.english: He is a person with strong self-control.

examples.japanese: {怒|おこ}りそうになったが、{自制心|じせいしん}を{保|たも}った。
examples.english: I was about to get angry, but I maintained my self-control.

examples.japanese: ダイエット{中|ちゅう}は{自制心|じせいしん}が{試|ため}されるが、{甘|あま}いものを{見|み}ると{負|ま}けてしまう。
examples.english: While on a diet, your self-control is tested, but I lose when I see sweets.

notes:
USAGE:
Often discussed in the context of personal development, education, and emotional management. A lack of {自制心|じせいしん} is seen as a character flaw.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {自制心|じせいしん}が{強|つよ}い (to have strong self-control)
- {自制心|じせいしん}を{保|たも}つ (to maintain self-control)
- {自制心|じせいしん}を{失|うしな}う (to lose self-control)
- {自制心|じせいしん}が{働|はたら}く (self-control kicks in)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {忍耐力|にんたいりょく}: perseverance; endurance — focuses on tolerating hardship over time
- {我慢|がまん}: patience; endurance — more everyday term for holding back or tolerating something
